newsitem.title: ITALY: BOXING-ITALIAN IN SERIOUS CONDITION AFTER COLLAPSE.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-ITALIAN IN SERIOUS CONDITION AFTER COLLAPSE.

text.p: Italian middleweight boxer Fabrizio De Chiara was in a serious condition in hospital on Sunday after collapsing in the last round of an Italian title fight.
De Chiara, 25, previously unbeaten in a 12-fight career, collapsed at the end of his 12-round contest against Vincenzo Imparato in the western Italian port of Massa on Saturday.
He stood up after being stopped with a left and a right and then collapsed. De Chiara was carried out on a stretcher and the rest of the fight was abandoned.
He was taken to hospital in nearby Pisa where doctors diagnosed major internal bleeding and operated for four hours. They said his condition remained very serious.
Imparato said he had been stunned by the incident.
"I would rather have lost the fight and the title than undergo these awful hours for a friend," he said.
"I could not sleep last night. I just keep thinking about De Chiara. I didn't want to win the title like this."
The winner said the fight should have been stopped in the 11th round and he did not understand why de Chiara's corner, his trainer and manager, had failed to throw in the towel.
"I could see my opponent was exhausted and gasping for breath, weakened by fatigue," said Imparato, who had fought De Chiara before many times as an amateur.
